stem.text: The graph shows changes in percentage saturation of haemoglobin with oxygen in the blood of a human and of another animal. The partial pressure of carbon dioxide remains constant at $1.0\,\text{kPa}$ and the temperature is constant at $25\,{}^{\circ}\text{C}$.

stem.alt: Graph of percentage saturation of haemoglobin with oxygen against partial pressure of oxygen/kPa: human and animal S-shaped curves, human curve lies above and to the left of the animal curve

stem.text: Which conclusion is supported by the graph?

A.text: At $25\,{}^{\circ}\text{C}$ the affinity of haemoglobin for oxygen increases more in humans than in the animal.

B.text: Haemoglobin in the animal carries less oxygen than haemoglobin in the human.

C.text: Oxygen is more easily released from haemoglobin in animal muscle than in human muscle.

D.text: The Bohr effect in the haemoglobin of the animal is greater than in human haemoglobin.
